source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "ដំណាំសណ្តែកដី" (Peanut / Groundnut Cultivation handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, 2008, produced under Loan 2022-CAM(SF) (an ADB-financed project; the cover names a livelihood/agriculture-improvement program under this loan). Uploaded as a 14-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source B for crop/peanut in this knowledge base (Source A was a shorter ECOSORN leaflet processed in Batch 42).
text: Peanut varieties are grouped in the source into two broad growth-habit types: a bush/spreading type with a shorter growth duration of roughly 120 days, and a climbing/runner type with a longer growth duration of roughly 170 days. Good-quality seed pods are described as typically containing 2-3 seeds per pod, with a long, well-filled shell, thick shell wall, and high oil content, plus uniform, vigorous germination. The source recommends selecting a variety adapted to local climate and describes variety "G2" as a locally adapted line that has long been used by farmers in flood-recession riverside growing areas.
